content.user_title: Generate Unit Tests From Existing Code
content.value_statement: Writing useful tests takes time and often misses edge cases. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce tests that follow project conventions.
actual_capabilities: Reviews target code structure, inputs, outputs, and error paths.
Identifies common test frameworks across JavaScript, Python, Go, Java, and Ruby projects.
Drafts tests for happy paths, boundary cases, invalid inputs, and async behavior.
Matches local naming, directory, assertion, setup, and teardown conventions.
Suggests mocks for external dependencies and side effects.
limitations: It does not run tests unless the user asks the agent to execute project commands.
Generated tests may need edits for hidden business rules or private fixtures.
Coverage targets are recommendations, not guaranteed results.
It depends on available source files and existing test examples.

use_cases.title: Add Coverage For New Code
use_cases.description: Create initial unit tests for a new module while following the project's current test style.

use_cases.title: Expand Edge Case Testing
use_cases.description: Identify boundary values, invalid inputs, and error paths that need stronger assertions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Test Patterns
use_cases.description: Help teams apply consistent naming, structure, and mocking patterns across services.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Basic Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use test-generator on this file and draft unit tests for the main public functions.

prompt_templates.title: Match Existing Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Use test-generator for this module. Match the assertion style, file naming, and setup patterns from the existing test directory.

prompt_templates.title: Cover Error Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Use test-generator to add tests for edge cases, invalid inputs, async failures, and mocked dependencies in this component.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Coverage Upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Use test-generator to review this subsystem, identify missing coverage, and propose a prioritized test plan with representative examples.

output_examples.input: Generate tests for a parser utility with valid, empty, malformed, and boundary inputs.
output: A test outline grouped by parser behavior.
Cases for valid input, empty input, malformed input, and boundary values.
Notes about expected errors and fixtures to create.

output_examples.input: Improve tests for a user service that calls an external dependency.
output: A mock strategy for the external dependency.
Positive and negative test scenarios for service behavior.
Assertions for returned values, thrown errors, and dependency calls.

best_practices: Provide the target file and nearby tests so the agent can match local conventions.
Ask for edge cases and error paths, not only happy path tests.
Review generated tests before committing, especially mocks and expected values.
anti_patterns: Using generated tests without checking that assertions match real requirements.
Requesting broad coverage without naming the target module or behavior.
Adding fragile tests that depend on implementation details instead of public behavior.

faq.question: Which test frameworks can this skill recognize?
faq.answer: It lists Jest, Mocha, Vitest, pytest, unittest, Go testing, Testify, JUnit, TestNG, RSpec, and Minitest.

faq.question: Can it create tests for a whole project?
faq.answer: It can plan broad coverage, but focused file or module requests usually produce better results.

faq.question: Does it execute the generated tests?
faq.answer: No. It generates tests and guidance. Ask the agent separately if you want test commands executed.

faq.question: Will it guarantee 80 percent coverage?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends that goal, but actual coverage depends on code, tests, and measurement tools.

faq.question: Can it mock external dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs the agent to identify side effects and suggest mocks for external dependencies.

faq.question: Is it safe for private codebases?
faq.answer: The skill itself contains only guidance. Users should still follow their organization's data handling policies.
